title: The Dress
hook: One photo of one dress, and the internet could not agree on its colours.
peek: In February 2015 a blurry photo of a dress split the internet. Some people saw white and gold, others blue and black, and each side could not believe the other. It was blue and black.
lede: In February 2015, a photo of a striped dress, taken in an English shop by the mother of a bride, was posted on Tumblr by a friend at the Scottish wedding and spread around the world in hours. Some people saw white and gold. Others saw blue and black. Each group could hardly believe the other. The real dress was blue and black, but that turned out to be the least interesting part.

bullets.text: Your brain constantly adjusts colours for the light it thinks is falling on them. The photo gives few clues about that light, so different brains make different guesses.

If you assume the dress sits in bluish shadow, your brain subtracts blue and you see white and gold. Assume warm indoor light, and it looks blue and black. Studies found people's assumptions predicted what they saw.
One study suggested early risers, who spend more time in daylight, were somewhat more likely to see white and gold. It is a tendency, not a rule.
In May 2015 the journal Current Biology published three separate studies of the photo together, one sign of how quickly vision scientists took a viral argument seriously.
